newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas futures called higher on OTC.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas futures called higher on OTC.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Monday, helped by firmer over-the-counter trade and some cooler temperatures in Texas and the West, industry sources said.
March over-the-counter traded early at $2.23 per million British thermal units, then was offered later at $2.23 and bid at $2.20. On Friday, March settled 17.9 cents lower at $2.182.

"Storage is low in the producing region and in the West, so every time we get some weather there, we're going to rally," said one Midwest trader, noting some technical buying after last week's selloff also may help lift the complex.
But despite the bounce today, most said they expected the upside move to be short-lived, particularly with little extreme weather forecast for the U.S. this week.

And while the market may be oversold and due for a bounce, technical traders said March's close Friday below trendline support could soon mean a test of the Nov 5 low of $2.12. March resistance was seen in the low-$2.50s and then in the $2.70 and $2.80 area.

In Friday cash, Gulf Coast prices skidded 10-15 cents to the mid-$2.30s. Midcon pipes were off about a nickel to the $2.30-35 area. New York city gate gas was quoted more than 10 cents lower at about $2.90.
